title: InSeasonOpportunityRecord
description: One player on the in-season Opportunity Board: the intrinsic rest-of-season estimate beside documented fantasy-market BEHAVIOUR. The behaviour signals are add and drop counts over a declared lookback window from a declared snapshot - they are not a price, not an ADP, not a rank, and no field here is subtracted from a rank (roadmap 10.3, 12.3). Behaviour may decide whether a player is surfaced; it may never change a single intrinsic number, and the artifact carries the intrinsic values unmodified from ros_tiers.json so that is checkable rather than promised.

ros_fair_rank.description: The model's rest-of-season fair rank. Null only on an unprojected row (model_coverage = unprojected, contract 1.2, ADR-102): no validated output exists for him, and none is invented.

ros_vorp_p50.description: Median simulated remaining VORP: the statistic `ros_fair_rank` orders by and the number the rest-of-season board draws, copied verbatim like every intrinsic column here. The Opportunity Board prints this rather than the mean, so a row's value and its rank are one account and a player carries one ROS value on every tab (ADR-097). For a surfaced row it is the value the untruncated board gave him, never a fill.

behavior_source_id.description: Which behaviour feed supplied the counts. `sleeper` in Release 2.

behavior_available.description: False when the optional behaviour capture was unavailable or stale. The board still publishes every intrinsic number: a failed behaviour source degrades this column, never the rest-of-season estimate (roadmap 12.5).

behavior_snapshot_at_utc.description: When the snapshot was taken. Sleeper publishes no observation time of its own, so this is the retrieval time and is recorded as such rather than presented as a data-as-of claim.

behavior_lookback_hours.description: The lookback window REQUESTED. Sleeper publishes nothing about the window it actually used, so the record describes the request (ADR-062's discipline, applied to behaviour).

behavior_request_limit.description: The row limit requested. Sleeper caps each trending feed at 100 rows whatever is asked (ADR-114), so a player absent from a feed is OUTSIDE ITS TOP 100 - an unknown count, never a zero. add_state and drop_state say which side was observed.

add_count.description: Rosters that added this player inside the lookback window, as the add feed reported it. Non-null exactly when add_state is `observed` (contract 1.3, ADR-114); a player outside the feed's top 100 publishes null, never 0. A count of transactions, in transactions. Never a pick number and never converted into one.

drop_count.description: Rosters that dropped this player inside the lookback window. Non-null exactly when drop_state is `observed`; null, never 0, when he was outside the drop feed's top 100.

net_add_count.description: add_count minus drop_count, and EXACT: non-null only when both sides were observed (contract 1.3). Both sides are the same unit measured over the same window by the same feed, which is the only reason this subtraction is legitimate. With one side outside its feed there is no net, only the bound add_count_max/drop_count_max imply, and a consumer must label a bound as one.

add_state.description: Contract 1.3 (ADR-114): how the add feed saw this player. `observed`: in the feed; add_count is his count (a real zero is possible). `not_in_feed`: the feed was retrieved and he was outside its top 100 - unknown, at most add_count_max. `no_sleeper_id` / `ambiguous_sleeper_id`: no verified, unpoisoned Sleeper id, so the feed cannot reach him. `stale`: the newest capture is beyond the freshness window. `unavailable`: no capture, or this feed failed.

drop_state.description: The same states, for the drop feed. Tracked independently of add_state.

add_count_max.description: Set only when add_state is `not_in_feed`: the add feed's smallest count, an upper bound on his because each feed is a descending top-N list (a shorter limit returns an exact prefix; probe 2026-10-21). A bound, labelled as one wherever it is shown; never a count.

drop_count_max.description: The same bound for the drop feed: set only when drop_state is `not_in_feed`.

add_rank.description: This player's position in the add feed, 1 being the most added. An ordering of the behaviour feed itself; it is not a draft rank and is never differenced against `ros_fair_rank`.

snap_share_last3.description: Recent share of team offensive snaps: the role context that makes a promotion visible. A model input as well as context, and shown as such.

current_status.description: Current roster status. Annotation only, visually separate from every model input, and never a model feature.

surface_reasons.description: Why this player is visible: inside the intrinsic depth, or surfaced by current role/behaviour evidence. A surfaced player carries a fair rank the model computed and no tier.

employment_status.description: Contract 1.2 (ADR-102): the employment_evidence_v1 reading also published on player_status. unsigned = a verified free agent (FA): no current club, so no next game and never a current-week Start/Sit choice; any value on the row is the model's and assumes nothing about a destination. Null when the build computed no reading.

model_coverage.description: Contract 1.2 (ADR-102). projected: every intrinsic column is the model's, copied from ros_tiers or the untruncated board. unprojected: a verified off-roster player (unsigned, or signed only on Sleeper evidence) surfaced by add volume with no validated rest-of-season output; both ranks, the tier and every ros_* value are null, never zero.
